Chapter Seven: The Role of Inspired Action and Intuition
So, picture this: you've got your plans laid out, everything seems organized, but real abundance? It often asks for something more. It’s about being open to those moments of inspiration and intuition—that inner voice, those gentle nudges that whisper, “Hey, try this,” or “What if you took a chance on that?”
Acting on inspiration is totally different from just staying busy. Instead of running around out of fear or obligation, inspired action comes from a place of trust—and a sense that you’re actually aligned with something bigger. It's kind of like a sailor adjusting the sails, right? The sailor isn’t just moving for the sake of it—they’re tuning in, catching the wind, adapting with purpose.
So, how do you start taking more inspired action in your own life? Let’s walk through a few steps together.
First, create space for reflection. Make it a habit to pause and check in with yourself. When was the last time you just sat in quiet and listened for your own inner guidance?
Next, notice what energizes you. There’s usually something—an idea, a project, a conversation—that lights you up or sparks your curiosity. Pay attention to those moments; they’re often clues.
Then, don’t be afraid to act on small nudges. Sometimes it’s just a tiny step, but following that feeling can lead to the most surprising breakthroughs.
And maybe the hardest part— release attachment to the outcome. Focus on the action itself, not just the result. Trust that, by following your intuition, the right opportunities will unfold in their own time.
Here’s how this plays out in real life: imagine an entrepreneur who’s been stuck, not making any progress for months. One day, she feels this quiet urge to go to a local networking event—even though she’s not sure why. She listens to that nudge and goes. Turns out, she meets someone there who becomes a major business partner. The opportunity didn’t come from forcing things, but from being willing to act on that soft inner push.
When you follow inspired action, it usually feels easy—sometimes even joyful. It’s more about allowing things to happen, rather than pushing all the time. You move forward when it feels right, and you rest when it doesn’t.
Over time, you start to trust yourself more. You notice that abundance tends to flow when you’re tuned in and responsive, rather than just grinding through. So, why not give yourself permission to listen for those inner prompts—and see where inspired action might take you?
